# Manwë

> Manwë is the elder King of the Valar and rules the wind and the air.

*Valar — Lord of the West*

## Overview

Manwë is the chief of the Valar and the appointed king of Arda beneath Eru Ilúvatar.

## Identity

- **Title:** King of the Valar
- **Role:** Air, wind, sky and Eagles
- **Spouse / consort:** Varda
- **Familiar symbols:** eagle; wind; Taniquetil
- **Kindred:** Valar

## Names and Etymology

The name **Manwë** is used throughout Tolkien's published legends for this figure.
Where an alternative name is known, it is preserved here as a secondary epithet rather than treated as a separate character.

## Character and Domain

In the Ainulindalë and Valaquenta, Manwë is defined less as a mortal-style personage than as a divine power: a will, office and creative theme made visible.
The sphere associated with Manwë is **Air, wind, sky and Eagles**. Tolkien repeatedly presents the Valar through consorts, crafts, music, duties and the shape of their houses.

## Relationship to Middle-earth

The Valar are the Powers of the World who entered Arda after the Music of the Ainur. They oppose Melkor, preserve creation and generally act through delegated powers rather than constant direct rule.

## Selected Quotes

> Manwë is the elder King of the Valar and rules the wind and the air.

*The Silmarillion, Valaquenta.*

> The Valar, the Guardians of the World, are called the Powers of the World; they are the greatest of the Ainur who came to Arda.

*The Silmarillion, Valaquenta (condensed).*

> The Music of the Ainur brought Eä into being, and into its vision the Valar entered.

*The Silmarillion, Ainulindalë (condensed).*
